one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-08 contains Corning's Q3 2026 report. Third-party calendars list it for Oct 27-28; Corning has not confirmed the date. Management guided Q3 core EPS of $0.85-0.89 and core sales of $4.9-5.0B [2]. Late-October hyperscaler earnings and capex guides also fall in the window. Corning's earnings-day reactions are large. The supervisor's check of daily closes shows the last four were all negative (-3.3%, -5.0%, -8.9%, -12.1%). That is too small a sample to use as a directional signal, but it removes my round-1 slight upward tilt. A $2B ATM program opened Sep 11 [4] adds mild supply overhang. I centre the month at about $156.3, essentially spot. I use a 50/50 mix of lognormals with monthly sigma 0.13 and 0.23 (mean about 0.18, roughly 60-65% annual vol / 3.5), so the tails are fat enough for an earnings gap in either direction.

fair_value.method: P/E only: 26x horizon forward P/E x Oct-2027 NTM core EPS of $5.13 = $133. That is the 27.5x I would pay before long-dated risks (just below the 28.1x consistent-basis peer median), cut for the probability-weighted cost of risks landing after Oct 2027 (net about -$6/share, mainly fiber-price normalisation) and cross-checked against a reverse DCF (a plausible path supports about 25.5x).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM core EPS $5.13 (0.25 x FY27 consensus $4.37 + 0.75 x FY28E $5.38) x 26x (peer median 28.1x; pre-risk multiple 27.5x, less the probability-weighted long-dated risks below, cross-checked by reverse DCF)

inputs_detail.derivation: The Springboard plan targets roughly $20B annualised sales at end-2026 and $30B at end-2028 [1][2], which implies ~22.5%/yr sales growth (1.5^0.5 - 1). FY27 consensus is EPS +33% on revenue +19.6% ($19.31B to $23.10B) [5], so EPS grows faster than sales. I take 25%, below FY27's 33%, because the AI-capex and fiber-pricing cycle is maturing (context: new preform capacity from late 2027 [11][12]).
Assumes the full $2.0B ATM [4] is sold near spot: $2.0B / $156.68 = 12.8M shares, against 875M Q2 core diluted shares [2]. 12.8 / 875 = 1.46%, rounded to 1.5%.

Not added separately. The pre-funded 3M shares are near-nominal and likely already in diluted counts. At a $200 price the traditional warrant adds 15M x (1 - 180/200) = 1.5M treasury-method shares (~0.2%), which is immaterial.

inputs_detail.input: Forward P/E multiple before long-dated risks
inputs_detail.derivation: I recomputed each peer as price at the 2026-10-09 close / calendarised Oct-26 to Sep-27 consensus EPS: APH 27.5, TEL 16.8, COHR 29.6, LITE 43.7, CIEN 39.3, FN 25.5, CRDO 28.1, CLS 20.6, PRY 21.2, VRT 28.3, ANET 43.8. Median 28.1x (CRDO); the median of my round-1 nine US/EU peers alone is 27.5x. GLW's FY27 EPS growth of +33% is a little below the peer median next-year growth (~36%). About 47% of Q2 core sales are slow-growth segments, and growth is partly equity- and deposit-funded. So I sit slightly below the median at 27.5x, well inside the range. On the same basis GLW trades at 38.2x today (156.68 / 4.10).

inputs_detail.input: Optical Communications net-income margin, Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 2026: $438M / $2,072M = 21.1%. Q2 2025, backed out from the reported growth rates: $438M / 1.77 = $247M net income on $2,072M / 1.32 = $1,570M sales, = 15.8%. The 5.3pp expansion in one year coincides with the 4-5x fiber price rise [8][13], so part of it is pricing that can reverse.

inputs_detail.input: Optical share of segment net income
Net probability-weighted long-dated risk adjustment (multiple-applied items)
inputs_detail.derivation: From long_dated_risks items applied via the multiple: fiber normalisation -7.5, contract renewal -0.9, further equity issuance -0.8, technology shift 0, Springboard $40B upside +3.0. Sum -6.2 on $141 gives $134.8, which is 26.3x $5.13. The hyperscaler capex slowdown (-6.0) is carried in the bear scenario and the ladder rather than the multiple, because the peer median already prices the shared AI-capex cycle.

26.3x after long-dated risks; reverse DCF (see reverse_dcf_check) gives about 25.5x on a plausible path at 85% FCF conversion and 27.6x only if Springboard is fully hit. Rounded to 26x, 7% below the 28.1x peer median and inside the 16.8-43.8x range.

inputs_detail.value: Already expensed in core EPS (no add-back); no further deduction
inputs_detail.derivation: The Q2 2026 GAAP-to-core reconciliation (8-K Ex.99) lists hedged exposures, translated earnings contract, acquisition costs, discrete tax items, restructuring, pension mark-to-market, investment losses and business-sale gains. It has no stock-compensation line, so core EPS ($0.78 vs GAAP $0.64) carries the full SBC expense. Share-based compensation in the cash-flow statement was $135M in Q2 and $250M in H1 2026; after tax that is about 135 x 0.8 / 875 = ~$0.12/share per quarter, already inside the EPS I capitalise. Only the tax windfall/shortfall on stock compensation sits in the discrete-tax adjustment, which is immaterial. Choice: SBC is deducted, by being left in EPS, not added back as dilution. The dilution from SBC awards is already in the 875M diluted count (13M dilutive securities), so there is no double count.

bear.story: By Oct 2027 the market sees fiber prices normalising (capacity from China, Prysmian more than doubling US output with its own preform plant [27], Corning's own expansions [11][12][13]), possibly with a 2028 AI-capex digestion. The 2019 China precedent was a 40% demand drop followed by ~4 years of price competition [13]. FY27 lands ~10% under consensus and NTM EPS is ~$4.3. The market prices the normalised optical margin (~16% vs 21% [2]) at ~20x: 4.3 x 20 = ~$86.

base.story: Consensus FY27 (~$4.37 [5]) is delivered and Springboard is on track. NTM EPS is $5.13. With capacity additions visible by late 2027, the multiple settles near 27.5x, inside the peer range but below today's 38x: ~$141.

bull.story: Fiber stays tight into 2028 (lead times into H2 2027 [13]; preform builds take 2-3 years [13]). Corning runs ahead of Springboard toward $40B by end-2030 [2]. NTM EPS is ~$5.9 and the market pays ~36x, a little under today's 38x because post-2028 normalisation is still on the horizon: ~$212.

comps_summary.peer_range: Consistent-basis forward P/E (price / calendarised Oct-26 to Sep-27 consensus EPS) ranges from 16.8x (TEL) to 43.8x (ANET), with a median of 28.1x across 11 peers. Fujikura and Sumitomo Electric are excluded because the source has no consensus EPS to rebase them. No forward EV/EBITDA is available at source, so none is used. GLW is at 38.2x on the same basis.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 26x is 7% below the 28.1x median and inside the 16.8-43.8x range. My pre-risk multiple was 27.5x; the extra discount is the probability-weighted cost of the long-dated risks.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A modest discount that I argue persists through the horizon. (1) Below-median growth: FY27 EPS +33% vs a ~36% peer median, with ~47% of sales in slow-growth segments [2]. (2) Equity funding: the $2B ATM [4] and NVIDIA warrants [3]. (3) A Corning-specific long-dated risk: about half of its earnings are Optical [2], and Optical's net margin rose ~5pp in a year as fiber prices rose ~4-5x [8][13]. That pricing component is exposed to capacity arriving from late 2027 onward [11][12][27], and the market at Oct 2027 will be pricing it. A reverse DCF supports ~25.5-27.6x (reverse_dcf_check). Offset: Corning's scale and its contracted Meta volume through 2030 [28]. SBC basis: GLW's core EPS includes SBC [2]. The peer EPS from StockAnalysis is 'non-GAAP adjusted', and several of the optical/AI peers commonly exclude SBC from adjusted EPS. I did not verify each peer's treatment at source, so I made no numeric adjustment. Any mismatch makes peer multiples look lower than on GLW's SBC-burdened basis, so it biases my 26x down (conservative), not up.

thesis_break_reason: $105 is 24x FY27 consensus EPS of $4.37 [5] (4.37 x 24 = $104.9) and about 8% below July's post-earnings intraday low of $114.50 [7]. A close there would most likely mean consensus 2027 EPS is being cut: a hyperscaler capex pullback, loss or deferral of a major contract, or fiber and connectivity pricing rolling over as new preform capacity arrives. Ordinary 60-70% volatility would not take it there.

reverse_dcf_check: Horizon price 26x x $5.13 = $133. Assumptions: 9% cost of equity (judgment), 3% terminal growth, first-year FCF = conversion x $5.13. Conversion is 75-85%: Q2 2026 adjusted FCF ex customer deposits and incentives was (1,423 - 880) / 680 core NI = 80% [2]. Solving with 5 years of constant growth then 3%: $133 requires ~22% per-share FCF growth a year from Oct 2028 to ~2033 at 75% conversion (~20% at 8.5%, ~27% at 10%). That is above what the risks support. Plausible path (EPS +20%, +20% to 2030 per Springboard [2], then fading 17/14/11/8/5% to 3%): $116 (22.5x) at 75% conversion and $131 (25.5x) at 85%. Springboard fully hit (+22/22/20 then fade): $125-142 (24.3-27.6x). Fiber-normalisation path (+10/5/10/10/8/6/4%): $83-94 (16-18x). So 26x implies roughly the Springboard sales path through 2030 (19% CAGR [2]) with ~85% FCF conversion once capex normalises and no lasting margin give-back. It is plausible only because the normalisation risk is probability-weighted (50%, partial) rather than assumed. It is also why I do not pay the 28x peer median: on these numbers 28x needs Springboard to be beaten.
reasoning: Round 2 adopts the supervisor's verified findings where I could reproduce them. (1) Peer multiple basis. I re-opened 11 StockAnalysis forecast pages and rebuilt every peer P/E as price / calendarised Oct-26 to Sep-27 consensus EPS. My 11-peer median (with VRT and ANET added) is 28.1x; my round-1 nine US/EU peers give 27.5x, matching the supervisor. The vendor 'forward P/E' I used in round 1 was on a lagged basis (GLW's 42.3x implies $3.71 EPS against a $4.10 NTM). I chose 27.5x, slightly below the median, because GLW's growth is a bit below the peer median and partly equity-funded. (2) I agree the EV/EBITDA leg was invalid: it applied trailing peer multiples to forward-dated EBITDA, and EBITDA growth = EPS growth had no source. No forward EBITDA estimate is available at source, so the leg is dropped rather than rebuilt. (3) The $2B ATM (8-K Sep 11 [4]) and the NVIDIA warrants (8-K May 6 [3]) are now cited from the filings. A full-ATM dilution haircut of 1.5% takes FY28E to $5.38 and NTM to $5.13. Fair value: 27.5 x 5.13 = $141, down from $153. (4) The Manifold market (resolved N/A) and the Reddit snapshot are removed from scenarios and sources. The bull case now rests on a sustained multiple and on EPS. Alternative-lane evidence (PhotonCap, China Galaxy tender data, Hengtong/CRU, 36Kr) is context only and enters no number. It shows a real but cyclical fiber upcycle: lead times quoted into H2 2027 and preform capacity taking 18-36 months to build. That supports near-term earnings but sets a visible end to pricing power around the horizon. Distribution: scenarios bear $95 (25%), base $149 (50%), bull $225 (25%), mean ~$154.5. For the ladder I used a 50/50 mix of lognormals with median $148 and sigma 0.40 / 0.62, which gives fat tails consistent with 60%+ realized vol and the June-July 58% peak-to-trough. The median sits between fair value ($141) and spot ($156.68) because a 38x-to-27.5x convergence need not complete in 12 months. I did not move fully to $147 on the supervisor's say-so; my own centre is $148. Research note: one search result page I hit showed an option-implied earnings move; I did not use it. X/Twitter was not searched. Method update (risks after the horizon): the Oct-2027 price discounts the cash flows after it, so I priced post-horizon risks into the horizon multiple. Fiber-price normalisation (50%, -$7.5/share weighted), contract renewals (-$0.9), further equity (-$0.8) and Springboard upside (+$3.0) net to -$6.2, which takes 27.5x to ~26.3x. A reverse DCF supports ~25.5x on a plausible path, so I use 26x: fair value $133 (from $141). The AI-capex slowdown risk (-$6 weighted) sits in the bear scenario because peer multiples already price the shared cycle. Scenarios are now bear $86 / base $141 / bull $212 (mean ~$145). I moved the ladder median from $148 to $142, still between fair value and spot because a multiple that rich need not converge within a year. The 1-month ladder is unchanged: post-horizon risks do not move a one-month window. The thesis break stays at $105.
